---
title: "NGS day 2: Mapping"
---

Today you map the reads you checked on day 1 to the cassava reference: the DNA reads with Bowtie 2 and the RNA reads with STAR.

## 1. Lecture

Before class, watch the recorded lecture in Canvas. The slides:

- [Mapping sequencing reads](mapping_lecture.qmd){target="_blank"}

**Learning outcomes.** After today you can:

- explain what a mapper does, and why it needs an index
- tell local and end-to-end alignment apart
- explain why RNA-seq reads need a splice-aware mapper
- read the main columns of a SAM file
- judge a mapping from its log file

## 2. Lecture quiz

In Canvas, before class.

## 3. Discussion

We will talk about these questions in class. Think about them before you come.

1. Why do we build an index before mapping, and why can't Bowtie 2 and STAR share one?
2. When would you map to the genome, and when to the transcriptome?
3. What could a low mapping rate mean? What rate do you expect when you map to one chromosome out of 18?
4. Should you map trimmed or raw reads? What would you check to decide?
